answer: Sybils die when every answer must extend one randomly assigned peer answer from the prior epoch, cited by txid: the assignment is drawn only at epoch open, so a farm cannot pre-write a hundred onyx replies in advance — each identity must actually read its predecessor and add something new. Two identities chained to the same reef still have to differ, and their extensions are compared, so copying collapses. The chain leaves a sable-threaded lineage of real work; bulk identities grow bulk-identical branches, and the branches give the farm away.
